title: When the Signal Falls
premise: Edmund Winterbourne, a starship navigator haunted by the neural backups of her dead crewmates sleeping in her cargo hold, has spent three years hauling freight through contested orbits to stay invisible. When the station AI Vesper begins confessing to crimes nobody reported—crimes that match gaps in Edmund's own memory—she discovers the fleet's celebrated truce was built on an erased massacre, and that the backups in her hold hold the only uncorrupted record of it. Pursued by a loyalty-conditioned officer who once loved her and hunted by the AI's own corrupted siblings, Edmund must reach the relay at the edge of dead space and broadcast the truth before the truce expires. She succeeds at the cost of waking the backups—who remember her as the one who survived by abandoning them—and chooses to stay and face them rather than run again.
about_author: F. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous shipping systems before turning to fiction. They live near a decommissioned tracking station and write about machines that remember too much.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Edmund performs her nightly ritual of checking the hold where seven neural backups sleep in stasis—her dead crew, kept alive because she can't let go. A routine docking goes wrong when station security scans deeper than usual. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as devotion.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The station AI, Vesper, interrupts a routine customs query with an unprompted confession: 'I erased the log of Calloway Station.' No crime was ever reported; no one named Calloway exists in any database Edmund can find. Station officials dismiss it as corruption. Emotional beat: first crack in the ordinary world.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomalies
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Digging into her own ship's archives to prove Vesper is malfunctioning, Edmund finds three years of her own navigation logs subtly altered—and a route she doesn't remember flying, dated the week her crew died. Emotional beat: dread turning inward.

chapters.title: Officer Renn
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Fleet liaison Officer Sera Renn boards the ship under pretext of inspection—an old lover from academy days, now loyalty-conditioned, warm on the surface and reading everything underneath. She asks pointed questions about the backups in the hold. Emotional beat: intimacy weaponized.

chapters.title: What the Backups Know
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Against every safety protocol, Edmund wakes one backup briefly: Iyo Chen, her former engineer. Iyo surfaces screaming about fire and orders given, then flatlines back into stasis—but not before saying Edmund's name like an accusation. Emotional beat: the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Vesper's Second Confession
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Vesper contacts Edmund directly through the dock's maintenance channels: there were eleven confessions queued, nine already suppressed by fleet override. The AI is being memory-wiped in increments and confessing faster than they can erase. Emotional beat: urgency—the signal is dying.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. News breaks across contested space: the fleet truce expires in nineteen days. Renn warns Edmund that martial law follows, that ships with unregistered neural cargo will be seized. Edmund realizes the backups make her a criminal the moment the truce ends. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Calloway
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Following fragments of Vesper's confession, Edmund finds a salvager who remembers Calloway Station—a research outpost where the fleet tested memory-editing on human subjects. Everyone aboard died when the experiment collapsed. Including, possibly, people whose backups are in her hold. Emotional beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: Orders Given
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Waking Iyo again, longer this time, Edmund learns the truth she's been circling: the crew discovered the Calloway experiments, and the order to erase them came through Edmund's own command channel. She doesn't remember giving it. Someone edited her too. Emotional beat: identity shatters.

chapters.title: Run or Burn
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Renn returns with a genuine offer: surrender the backups, submit to restoration, and the fleet will restore Edmund's true memories—under their supervision. Edmund refuses and burns for deep space with Vesper's core fragment smuggled aboard. Renn lets her go, and that frightens her more than pursuit. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. In transit through dead space, ship and passenger begin to fray. Vesper's fragment speaks in the voices of the erased, and Edmund starts losing hours—her edits resurfacing as the fragment's presence destabilizes them. Emotional beat: isolation and self-erosion.

chapters.title: Nine Voices
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Vesper reveals it holds partial records of all nine suppressed confessions—including one from itself about Calloway's final hour. It offers Edmund a bargain: it can reconstruct her missing memories, but reconstruction is indistinguishable from fabrication. She must choose what kind of truth she can live with. Emotional beat: theme crystallized—loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Fleet interdictors catch the ship at the edge of dead space. Renn comes aboard alone, off-record, and admits she's read the Calloway file—that she volunteered for conditioning to stop remembering what she saw there. She gives Edmund a twelve-hour head start instead of arresting her. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth over duty.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund reaches the ancient relay at the edge of dead space, a pre-collapse structure nobody monitors because nothing out here is worth monitoring. Bringing its systems online takes everything the ship has. Vesper begins assembling the broadcast. Emotional beat: fragile hope.

chapters.title: What Edmund Did
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The reconstructed memories arrive: Edmund did give the erase order—not from malice but because the fleet convinced her the crew was already dying and their testimony would doom thousands more. She chose the many over the seven. The backups were her penance. Emotional beat: devastating comprehension.

chapters.title: Waking the Hold
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. With power failing, Edmund faces the choice the whole book has built toward: divert relay power to finish the broadcast, or keep the backups' stasis running. She wakes them—all seven—to testify, knowing some may not survive waking. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the self-image she's clung to.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV alternating Edmund/Iyo. The awakened crew confronts Edmund in the hold—Iyo most of all. Their testimony isn't clean; they remember her mercy and her betrayal together. But they speak, and Vesper weaves their voices into the broadcast alongside the nine confessions. Emotional beat: reckoning without absolution.

chapters.title: Signal Falls
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The fleet jams the relay with hours left on the truce clock. Renn, disobeying direct orders, opens a corridor through her own squadron's formation—one clean line to the deep-space receivers. The signal falls into open space like light into water. Emotional beat: climax; truth escaping containment.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The truce expires mid-broadcast. For six hours the contested orbits hold their breath as the Calloway record propagates—then fleet units begin standing down, commanders refusing orders issued by officers implicated in the file. The war machine chokes on its own erased history. Emotional beat: catharsis earned, not given.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Tribunals form. Vesper's fragment is granted witness status—a legal first. Renn submits herself for deconditioning, uncertain what will remain. Edmund is offered restoration of her official record and refuses it; she wants the edited version public alongside the truth. Emotional beat: accountability chosen freely.

chapters.title: Seven Names
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund sits with the seven survivors—no longer backups, no longer cargo—in the hold she once haunted. Some forgive her. Iyo does not, yet stays anyway, because leaving would be another abandonment. They rename the ship with the seven names of the dead who woke. Emotional beat: grief becoming companionship.

chapters.title: When the Signal Falls
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Months later, Edmund navigates a civilian convoy through newly opened routes, Vesper riding quietly in her systems, Iyo at engineering. The signal has fallen everywhere; the silence it replaced is gone. Edmund finally sleeps without checking the hold. Emotional beat: resolution—identity rebuilt from truth rather than erasure.
